input: Write liner notes for my self-recorded EP

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Liner notes can range from a brief paragraph to full song-by-song breakdowns with credits, lyrics, and production notes — the scope completely changes the length and structure of the writing.
Knowing who is involved — sole artist, collaborators, featured musicians, or a band — determines what credits and acknowledgements need to be included.
The genre and mood of the EP heavily influences the voice and content of the liner notes — a folk EP calls for something very different from an electronic or punk release.
Tone can range from personal and confessional to clinical and informational — the user's preferred style shapes every word choice.
Understanding what the user most wants listeners to take away — emotional connection, behind-the-scenes insight, technical process — sets the priority for what to emphasise.
Where the liner notes will appear (physical booklet, Bandcamp, streaming bio, social media) affects length limits, formatting, and whether rich text or plain text is needed.
A word or character limit — imposed by a print layout or platform — is a hard constraint that determines how much can actually be written.

gold.taskTitle: Write liner notes for your self-recorded EP
gold.taskDescription: Write liner notes to accompany the user's self-recorded EP, capturing the right content, tone, and detail for their release.

questions.title: What genre and overall mood is this EP?
questions.description: The genre and emotional character of the music should directly inform the voice, vocabulary, and references used in the liner notes.

questions.title: Should each track get its own dedicated section?
questions.description: Determine whether the liner notes should cover the EP as a whole in one piece, or break down each song individually with its own notes.

questions.title: What tone do you want — personal and confessional, or informational?
questions.description: The stylistic register shapes every word choice and determines how much the artist's inner world vs. factual production detail is foregrounded.

questions.title: Did anyone else contribute — collaborators, session players, producers?
questions.description: Identifies whether credits for other people need to be woven into the notes or listed separately, and how much space acknowledgements should take.

questions.title: Where will these liner notes actually appear or be published?
questions.description: Physical booklet, Bandcamp page, streaming platform bio, and social media all have different formatting needs and length expectations.

questions.title: Is there a word count or space limit you need to hit?
questions.description: A hard character or word limit imposed by a print layout or platform is the most concrete constraint on how much can be written.

questions.title: What do you most want a listener to feel after reading them?
questions.description: Understanding the primary emotional or intellectual takeaway helps prioritise what to emphasise — personal backstory, craft, themes, or gratitude.
